newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Trucked airfreight leaps in Q1 at Cointrin airport.
newsitem.headline: Trucked airfreight leaps in Q1 at Cointrin airport.

text.p: Geneva's Cointrin airport handled 10,404 tonnes of trucked airfreight in the first quarter of 1997, representing an increase of 34.1 percent on 1996 levels, airport authority figures showed.

The growth in trucked airfreight was probably largely due to Swissair offering less belly-capacity on long-haul passenger routes from Geneva and with the airline shipping more cargo between the airport and Zurich by road, an airport authority official told Reuters.
Meanwhile, flown airfreight handled at Geneva fell by 10.1 percent to 14,697 tonnes on the same period last year, airport figures also showed.
Swissair operates a three-times-weekly full-freighter service between Geneva and Singapore, with stopovers at Dubai and Madras, using a 67-tonne capacity McDonnell Douglas DC10-30F aircraft.
Postal traffic in the first quarter fell by 3.6 percent on the first three months of 1996 to 2,133 tonnes.
